chapter: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
title: First stay in New York, Roger Wolfe Kahn's club and Redman
summary: During a month in New York they heard Kahn's band at his society club, and Challis comments on Redman's influence.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: This is your first stay in New York of any length, and what were some of the things that were happening that you absorbed there besides hearing Fletcher.

Well, I heard Fletcher and then one night, we went over to the Paracade to Par to hear Roger -- we had been invited over there and he had a very high faluting club, you know, there were fish in the tables and he had put the lights on them and where he had the band, and you could see the fish and then he'd put them out and the floor was lighted up and it was sort of a society place.

Anyway when we went in we had to go in the back way and we sat in the back of the band, off on the side where the waiters went back and forth in front of us. There was Trumbauer and Bix and I and I think a couple other guys. This was our first experience at hearing the band close. He didn't have that band too long, I think only a year or two.

But we were very happy to go to hear it, and then of course Jimmy came around. Murray took sick and Jimmy made a couple of records with us. Let's see I think it was the second time Danny Polo (phonetic) came and played. He made "My Pretty Girl" with us. So I didn't make a point of going around and hear too many bands, to tell you the truth. [They'd] go up to Harlem.
Do you think Redman had any effect
on you or Fletcher hearing those things. folks?
Just appreciated them for what they were and you had your own --
I had never heard of Redmond Redman before until I met him there, and I don't think our arrangements are anything alike at all. But --
Sometimes you can get something from someone and you don't go over to their style but yet, you hear something and something seeps in.
